name: Varda
description: Varda is privately held and has no ticker. Review its funding rounds and valuations, the investors that hold its shares, and the points to confirm before buying or selling.
ledes: Varda Space Industries is a privately held space manufacturing company. Its shares are not listed on an exchange and have no quoted market price; the principal public reference points are the valuations at which the company has raised capital. Its most recent financing, a $250 million Series D round announced on September 30, 2026, valued the company at $1.6 billion.

Founded in 2021 and based in El Segundo, California, Varda builds spacecraft that process pharmaceutical compounds in orbit and return them to Earth in reentry capsules. Existing shares change hands in privately negotiated transactions and remain subject to the company's transfer restrictions.
table_note: Valuations are as reported at the time of each round. The Series D valuation is as reported by Reuters; Varda did not disclose a valuation for its Series C.
round_notes: With the Series D announcement, Varda said its total funding had reached $598 million; that figure is the company's own.

A round valuation reflects the terms of the preferred stock issued in that round. Most shares sold by employees are common stock, which carries fewer rights and typically trades at a discount to the preferred price.
investors: Lux Capital and Natural Capital led the Series D, with participation from Khosla Ventures, General Catalyst, Founders Fund and Caffeinated Capital. Natural Capital and Shrug Capital led the Series C, and Caffeinated Capital led the Series B in April 2024. Other investors include Peter Thiel and Also Capital.
spv_sentence: SEC filings show one special purpose vehicle formed to invest in Varda, organized in 2026.
sources: Sources: Varda's company page; reports by Payload (September 2026), Los Angeles Business Journal (October 2026), Reuters (September 30, 2026), CNBC (July 2025) and TechCrunch (April 2024); and SEC Form D filings.
